Beninese Festival Goat and Fish Stew

Served at: Fete du Vodoun (Benin Vodoun Festival)

Serves 6-8Prep 30 minCook 2 hours

This hearty stew is a staple during Fête du Vodoun, a vibrant annual celebration in Benin that honors the Vodoun deities and ancestral spirits. It embodies the spirit of communal feasting, combining tender goat meat and delicate fish in a rich, flavorful palm oil and tomato-based sauce, often served with fufu or rice as a symbol of abundance and community.

Ingredients

  • 3.3 lbs (1.5 kg) goat meat, bone-in or boneless, cut into 2-inch pieces
  • 1.1 lbs (500 g) firm white fish fillets (e.g., tilapia, snapper), cut into large chunks
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) red palm oil
  • 2 large onions, chopped
  • 4 cloves garlic, minced
  • 1-inch piece fresh ginger, grated
  • 1 (14.5 oz / 400g) can diced tomatoes, undrained, or 4-5 ripe fresh tomatoes, chopped
  • 1 red bell pepper, deseeded and chopped
  • 1 green bell pepper, deseeded and chopped
  • 1-2 Scotch bonnet or habanero peppers, whole or minced (adjust to taste, optional)
  • 2 cups (about 7 oz / 200g) fresh okra, trimmed and sliced
  • 2 bouillon cubes (chicken or vegetable), crushed
  • 1 teaspoon salt, or to taste
  • 1/2 teaspoon black pepper, or to taste
  • 4 cups (960 ml) water or goat broth

Method

  1. Season the goat meat with a pinch of salt and pepper. In a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven, heat 2 tablespoons of the palm oil over medium-high heat. Brown the goat meat in batches until lightly seared on all sides. Remove the goat meat and set aside.
  2. Add the remaining palm oil to the pot. Reduce heat to medium. Add the chopped onions and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
  3. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger, cooking for another 2 minutes until fragrant.
  4. Add the diced tomatoes (or fresh chopped tomatoes), red bell pepper, green bell pepper, and whole or minced Scotch bonnet pepper (if using). Cook for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables soften and the sauce thickens slightly.
  5. Return the seared goat meat to the pot. Add the water or broth and the crushed bouillon cubes. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until the goat meat is very tender. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
  6. After the goat meat is tender, add the sliced okra to the stew. Continue to simmer, uncovered, for about 15 minutes, or until the okra is tender and the stew has thickened to your desired consistency.
  7. Gently add the fish chunks to the stew, submerging them in the sauce. Cook for another 10-15 minutes, or until the fish is opaque and flakes easily. Be careful not to overcook the fish.
  8. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed. Remove the whole Scotch bonnet pepper before serving if you prefer less heat.
  9. Serve hot with fufu, banku, eba, or steamed rice.

Tips

  • For a richer flavor, marinate the goat meat overnight with some garlic, ginger, and a pinch of salt.
  • If fresh okra is unavailable, frozen sliced okra can be used; add it directly to the stew without thawing.
  • The stew can be made a day ahead; the flavors often meld and improve overnight. Reheat gently, adding a splash of water if needed.
